text:
ops-lead: Heads up — scheduling a short rolling reboot window to address intermittent egress oscillations we saw on apac-west1 and eu-central racks. Window: Wed 02:00–06:00 UTC. Plan is sequential cohorts (rack-by-rack), keep <=10% GPU capacity offline at any time. Canary first, then ramp.

ruth: Which exact pools are in-scope? Any Dedicated customers affected?

ops-lead: In-scope: apac-gpu-pool-a (high traffic), apac-gpu-pool-b (spill/backfill), eu-gpu-pool-x. Dedicated capacity will be routed to pinned fallback pools where possible; we will not evict reserved workloads but might re-route burst traffic.

kai: Canary plan? KV cache/warmup concerns?

ops-lead: Canary = 1 rack (apac-gpu-pool-a cohort-1) at 02:00 for 20–30m. Steps: cordon -> drain -> reboot BMC -> smoke tests -> uncordon. KV cache: we will pre-seed common prefixes to avoid cold-cache latency. After uncordon we run a small kv-seed job for 10m.

ops-lead: Drain command (example):
```
kubectl drain node-apac-rack12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=15m
```

sam: Cost/latency tradeoffs? We should estimate impact for product teams.

ops-lead: Expect a temporary ~3–6% p50 latency climb for apac while backfill shifts work and caches re-warm. Token-cost bump estimated ~5–8% for the window due to spill into less-optimized variants. Proposal: throttle interruptible tenants by 30% during cohorts to reduce cost.

matt: We'll get a spike of noisy alerts from e2e health checks — what to mute?

ops-lead: Mute: `egress-packet-loss-apac-west1` for 40m, and `kv-cache-hit-drop` for 20m on the canary rack. Do not mute `node-unhealthy` or `gpu-temperature` alerts. Post-mute we should resume strict alerting and run targeted postmortem checks.

infra-bot: preflight checks: network baseline OK, 95th percentile egress stable, no pending NIC firmware patches blocking this window.

ops-lead: Timing and owners:
- 01:30 UTC: final preflight (ops-lead + oncall)
- 02:00 UTC: canary cordon/drain (kai + oncall)
- 02:30 UTC: canary smoke tests (ruth)
- 03:00–05:30 UTC: staggered cohorts (sam + infra)
- 05:30–06:00 UTC: final verification + unmute alerts (ops-lead)

oncall: I can be onsite for canary, will have runbook open.

ops-lead: Links: runbook (internal) + short checklist will be posted to #release-war-room before 01:45. Also will open a brief incident-thread for timeline.

deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance job created: maintenance/1774131415-egress-oscillation-mitigation (eta 02:00 UTC).

sam: I'll shift autoscaling thresholds to be slightly more aggressive on apac pools during the window to help absorb traffic. Also enabling KV prefix caching for top-200 prefixes.

kai: After canary, if packet-drop persists we abort further cohorts and roll back to current routes. We should have a fallback model variant ready (lower mem, but stable egress) — @ops-lead please confirm.

ops-lead: Confirmed — fallback variant (v1-stable) is ready and routable. Abort criteria: >1% sustained packet loss over 5m on canary + failed smoke tests.

matt: Noted — I'll patch monitoring dashboards to show cohort status and capacity margin (+ links).

ops-lead: OK — everyone set for Wed 02:00 UTC. Please RSVP with :thumbsup: if you can be available. ops-lead out.

ruth: :thumbsup: available for smoke tests.

kai: :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup: will throttle interruptible tenants as discussed.

oncall: Standing by.

matt: :thumbsup:

ops-lead: Great — starting preflight at 01:30 UTC. If anything changes I'll post immediate updates here.
